note: Curated catalog of open source video, image, and voice generation models, restricted to unconditionally free licenses only (Apache-2.0/MIT, no custom "community license", no MAU/revenue thresholds, no academic-only caveats). Verified via web search Aug 2026. Model ids are Hugging Face repo ids intended for DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained (video), AutoPipelineForText2Image/AutoPipelineForImage2Image.from_pretrained (image), or chatterbox's own <Variant>.from_pretrained(device) (voice — id documents which HF repo that variant loads, but isn't passed as an argument; `variant` is the actual class-selection key). Every entry's `media_type` ("video", "image", or "voice") determines which handler and default capabilities apply. VRAM figures are sourced from model cards/community benchmarks and vary with resolution/frame count/offloading; treat as approximate. Deliberately excluded despite being otherwise capable: ByteDance Waver 1.0 (not open-weight at all), MiniMax-H3 (license bars local deployment in the US/EU/UK/South Korea), AnimateDiff (README says "academic use" despite an Apache-2.0 tag), LTX-Video/LTX-2.5 (LTX Community License: free only under $10M revenue, bars training competing AI systems, bars competing products), CogVideoX-5B (CogVideoX License: requires commercial registration, capped at 1M visits/month), HunyuanVideo-1.5 (Tencent Community License: free only under 100M MAU).

magi_1_distilled.notes: Autoregressive chunk-based generation (predicts fixed-length video chunks sequentially, next chunk starts before current fully denoises) rather than single-shot diffusion — designed to hold up better over longer/more dynamic motion than same-tier single-shot models. 12GB figure requires window_size=1 in the distill+quant config.

wan2.1_1.3b.notes: Smallest member of the Wan family, explicitly built for consumer GPUs.

cogvideox_2b.notes: Smaller sibling of CogVideoX-5B — note the 5B is under the restrictive custom CogVideoX License, but the 2B was relicensed to Apache-2.0. Trained in FP16; quantizable further with PytorchAO/Optimum-quanto down to free-tier-Colab-class GPUs.

wan2.2_ti2v_5b.notes: Unified T2V+I2V in one checkpoint. ~27.4GB at FP16 for 25 frames @ 768x512; FP8 cuts ~40%. Very fast — a 5s 720p clip in under 9 minutes on a single consumer GPU.

wan2.2_a14b.params: 27B total / 14B active per step (MoE: high-noise + low-noise experts)
wan2.2_a14b.notes: First open source MoE video model. Default requires an 80GB-class GPU (A100/H100); --offload_model/--t5_cpu flags trade speed for lower VRAM but 80GB is the no-compromise figure.

mochi_1.notes: Very strong motion quality/coherence. ~60-70GB single-GPU at full precision for the full 163-frame length; the bf16 variant with ComfyUI-level optimization can run under 22GB, at reduced frame count/speed.

skyreels_v1.notes: Fine-tuned from HunyuanVideo on ~10M film/TV clips; best open option for human-centric cinematic quality (faces, expression, camera work).

magi_1_full.notes: Full, non-distilled version. Exact VRAM floor not confirmed via search; scaling from the 4.5B variant's ~24GB at standard precision implies an 80GB+ class requirement. Same autoregressive chunk-based architecture as magi_1_distilled, at full quality. min_vram_gb left null (excluded from matching) until a figure is confirmed.

flux_1_schnell.notes: Latency-distilled (4-step) rectified-flow transformer — trades a little fidelity for very fast single-image generation. min_vram_gb_quantized reflects int8 weight-only quantization (transformer + T5 text encoder), which runs comfortably on Apple Silicon (MPS) unified memory without CPU offload.

ssd_1b.notes: Distilled/pruned SDXL: ~50% fewer parameters and ~60% faster than base SDXL while staying pipeline-compatible (SDXL-architecture LoRAs and the standard img2img pipeline apply). Runs well on 8GB VRAM — usable down to 4-6GB at a significant speed cost, not treated as a separate tier here. The lightest model in this catalog; picked over flux_1_schnell on constrained hardware.

chatterbox_base.notes: Zero-shot voice cloning from a short (5-20s) reference clip via audio_prompt_path — every variant supports this, not a separate capability. English only. Community figures for VRAM range 8-16GB depending on generation length; 8GB used here as the conservative floor.

chatterbox_turbo.notes: Distilled for low-latency voice agents: single-step speech-token-to-mel decoding (vs. base's 10 steps), ~1GB VRAM at FP16. Same zero-shot voice cloning as base, trades some fidelity/expressiveness for speed. English only.

chatterbox_multilingual.notes: Same base architecture and voice-cloning capability as chatterbox_base, trained on 23 languages instead of English-only. Shares the same underlying HF repo as chatterbox_base (`variant` is what actually selects the class/weights, not `id`). VRAM not separately benchmarked — assumed comparable to base given the shared architecture.

ugc_product_review.notes: Pass reference images to additionally require image-to-video capability, for product fidelity.

commercial_product_ad.notes: Pass reference images to additionally require image-to-video capability, for product fidelity.

explainer_testimonial.notes: Pass a reference image to additionally require image-to-video capability, to anchor speaker/product identity.

presenter_avatar.notes: No catalog model currently has native audio/dialogue capability; this type has no viable model today.

social_short_form_ad.notes: Produces a silent visual only; dialogue/voice_tone are not fulfilled by generation itself.

music_video.notes: No catalog model currently supports audio-synced generation; this type has no viable model today.

motion_graphics.notes: No catalog model specifically targets abstract/graphic motion-design output; a match here is a fallback, not a genuine fit.
